h1: The 8 Best White Nightstands of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 white nightstands compared on size, drawer style, charging ports and weight capacity, from plain two-drawer to LED smart units.
summary: The SONGMICS BELLAH is the best white nightstand: five charging ports, a 66 lb capacity rating and an anti-tip kit for $25 to $50. The WLIVE three-drawer is the tallest pick at 29.5 inches, the BOLUO customizes, and the Yoobure is the only FCC and ETL certified model. The Sweetcrispy is the cheapest.
intro: A white nightstand looks simple until you compare what sits under the paint. Some have drawers, some have outlets, some have LED strips, and heights range from about 20 inches to nearly 30. A table that is the wrong height for your bed is a small annoyance you meet every single night, whether it is a reach too far up or a lamp that looks stranded below the mattress.

We reviewed eight current white nightstands on paper, focusing on dimensions, charging, drawer type and capacity. All but one use fabric drawers, which is typical for this price tier, and we ranked them on how well each solves a real bedside problem. Weight ratings, port counts and certification marks carried more weight than lighting effects.

products.name: SONGMICS BELLAH White 2-Drawer Nightstand with 5 Charging Ports
products.verdict: Five charging ports, a 66 lb capacity and an anti-tip kit in one tidy table.
products.description:
The BELLAH measures 15.6 by 11.8 by 23.8 inches and combines two drawers with two AC outlets, two USB-A ports and one USB-C port. It adds app-controlled LED with music sync and ships with an anti-tip kit. It sells for $25 to $50. Five ports is the most in this list, and the mix of AC and USB means a lamp and two chargers do not compete for the same outlet.

It wins because it has the most charging ports here and a stated 66 lb capacity, the strongest rating among the charging models. The LED is a bonus rather than the point. Against the WLIVE two-drawer, it adds two more ports and an anti-tip kit.

Buy it if your bedside needs power for several devices. The caveat is the particleboard and PVC leather construction, typical for the price tier, not solid wood. Skip it if you want a plain table with no electronics.
products.idealFor: Bedsides that need to power several devices.
products.skipIf: You want a plain, no-electronics table.

products.name: WLIVE White 3-Drawer Fabric Dresser Nightstand
products.verdict: The tallest pick at 29.5 inches, with three removable fabric drawers.
products.description:
WLIVE makes a 15.7 by 11.8 by 29.5 inch table, the tallest in this guide, with an MDF top, steel frame and three removable, foldable fabric drawers. It has no charging ports and sells for $25 to $50. The top is water-resistant, and the extra height lets it double as a slim dresser in a small bedroom.

It ranks second because height is a rare, useful trait: a raised bed needs a taller table, and this one fits more beds than any other here. The BELLAH has more features, but its 23.8 inch height suits average mattresses only. Against the Sweetcrispy's 20 inches, it stands almost ten inches taller.

Best for a bed with a high mattress. The caveat is no power, so you need a separate charger. Skip it if you want built-in power.
products.idealFor: High beds that need a taller table.

products.name: BOLUO White 2-Drawer Nightstand with LED and USB-C
products.verdict: Removable wooden handles, adjustable feet and LED with 20 plus colors.
products.description:
BOLUO measures 15.7 by 11.8 by 23.6 inches with two fabric drawers, two AC outlets, two USB ports and an LED with more than 20 DIY colors. Removable wooden handles and adjustable feet are the distinguishing details. It sells for $25 to $50. Adjustable feet matter on uneven floors, where a rigid table rocks every time you reach for a drawer.

It ranks third because the customizing is fun but the power count is lower than the BELLAH's five ports. The feet are a real edge, though, since none of the plain tables here offer them. Against the Somdot, it has the same height, with fewer certifications and more color options.

Best for a bedroom with character or old floorboards. The caveat is that LED options are a feature, not a core need. Skip it if you want a single plain look.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms with uneven floors or a custom style.
products.skipIf: You want a single plain look.

products.name: Yoobure White 3-Drawer Nightstand, FCC & ETL Certified
products.verdict: The only FCC and ETL certified pick, with an X-bar support frame.
products.description:
Yoobure measures 15.4 by 11.8 by 25.6 inches, with a solid wood frame, three fabric drawers, two USB and two AC ports. It lists 16 RGB colors, 22 modes, FCC and ETL certification, and an X-bar support frame. It sells for $25 to $50. An ETL mark means the wiring was assessed by a recognized lab, which matters for mains power inside bedroom furniture.

It ranks fourth because certification is a real reassurance beside a bed, but its feature count is lower than the BELLAH's. It is the only certified model in the field. Against the BOLUO, it trades adjustable feet for a safety mark and a sturdier X-bar frame.

Best for buyers who care about electrical safety marks. The caveat is that three fabric drawers hold lighter loads than a hard cabinet. Skip it if you want the most ports.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants certified bedside wiring.

products.name: WLIVE White 2-Drawer Nightstand with RGB LED, 3 USB Ports, 55 lb Capacity
products.verdict: Three USB ports, two AC outlets and a 55 lb capacity.
products.description:
WLIVE measures 15.67 by 11.73 by 25.19 inches with an MDF and steel build, two fabric drawers, three USB ports plus two AC outlets and an RGB LED controlled via the iStrip+ app. The top is waterproof, capacity is 55 lb, and it sells for $25 to $50. A waterproof top shrugs off a spilled glass, which a bare MDF surface does not.

It ranks fifth because it has strong capacity and port counts but sits behind the BELLAH and Yoobure in features. It beats the BOLUO on stated capacity, 55 lb against no rating, and the three-drawer WLIVE on power.

Best for bedsides with a heavier lamp or clock. The caveat is that the app is another thing to configure. Skip it if you avoid app-controlled lights.

products.name: Somdot White Leather Nightstand with Voice-Sync LED, FSC Certified
products.verdict: FSC certified with a lead-free coating and voice, app and music LED control.
products.description:
Somdot measures 15.7 by 11.8 by 23.6 inches with E1 MDF and a powder-coated steel frame, two fabric drawers, two AC outlets, one USB-A and one USB-C. The LED takes voice, app, timer and music control, and the build is FSC certified with a lead-free coating. It sells for $25 to $50. E1 is a low-formaldehyde board grade, which is useful in a bedroom.

It ranks sixth because the eco credentials are a genuine differentiator, but the LED focus is a niche need. It beats the JOONEE on charging, with two AC outlets and a USB-C against a single station. Against the Yoobure, it swaps electrical certification for material certification.

Best for buyers who care about materials. The caveat is a lower port count. Skip it if you do not want an LED feature.
products.skipIf: You do not want an LED feature.

products.name: Sweetcrispy White 2-Drawer Nightstand with Arch Handles
products.verdict: The cheapest here: two fabric drawers, a water-resistant top, no electronics.
products.description:
Sweetcrispy measures 18 by 11.8 by 20 inches with a metal frame and engineered wood, two fabric drawers, arch handles and an end-stop design that stops drawers pulling out. It has no charging ports and a 44 lb capacity, and sells for under $25. At 20 inches it is the shortest in this guide, which suits a low bed.

It ranks seventh only because it is the plainest. It is the cheapest in the list and the lowest-capacity pick that publishes a rating. The water-resistant top and end-stop drawers are practical touches at that price. Against the WLIVE three-drawer, it is nearly ten inches shorter and wider.

Best for a low bed and a small budget. The caveat is no power, and the 18 inch width takes more wall. Skip it if you want power at the bedside.
products.idealFor: Low beds on a small budget.
products.skipIf: You want power at the bedside.

products.name: JOONEE White Nightstand with Vertical Texture and Solid Pine Legs
products.verdict: Solid pine legs, a vertical texture finish and a built-in charging station.
products.description:
JOONEE measures 15.7 by 11.8 by 25.2 inches with MDF and solid pine legs, two drawers, a charging station and an open shelf. It adds LED atmosphere lighting, a vertical textured paint and anti-slip rubber pads, and sells for $50 to $100, the highest tier here. The open shelf keeps a book within reach without opening a drawer.

It ranks last because the design-forward look is the draw, not the specs. It is the only pick with genuine solid pine legs, which the others lack. Against the BELLAH, it costs a bracket more and lists no capacity, so you pay for style.

Best for a bedroom where looks come first. The caveat is that capacity is not highlighted. Skip it if you want a stated weight rating.
products.skipIf: You want a stated weight rating.

whatMatters.detail: A nightstand should sit within a few inches of the top of your mattress. In this guide heights range from about 20 to 29.5 inches. Measure from the floor to the top of your mattress before buying, and compare with the listing, since a table that is too low makes you bend and too high strains your shoulder.

A phone, lamp and tablet need at least three sockets. AC outlets power lamps and USB ports charge devices. Count your devices and pick a table with more ports than you need today. The BELLAH offers five, the Sweetcrispy none, and a stray power strip defeats the point of a clean bedside. Count a charging cable for a watch or earbuds too.

Wiring inside furniture should carry an electrical safety mark such as ETL. Only the Yoobure lists FCC and ETL here. If you care about it, check the listing for named certification, not vague words like safe or approved. Uncertified wiring beside a bed is a risk worth avoiding, and a lab-assessed model costs little extra.

Most picks use fabric drawers, which are light and removable but not for heavy items. Plan to keep books and small items inside, not weight. Check capacity ratings: the BELLAH lists 66 lb, the WLIVE two-drawer 55 lb and the Sweetcrispy 44 lb. A missing rating deserves a question, and heavy lamps belong on the top, not in a drawer.

Anti-tip kits and adjustable feet help on uneven floors and around kids. The BELLAH includes an anti-tip kit and the BOLUO has adjustable feet. Check the listing for them, and anchor a tall table to the wall if children share the room, since slim legs tip easily. Keep cords tidy so a child cannot pull the table over.

faq.q: What height should a nightstand be?
faq.a: Roughly level with the top of your mattress, give or take a few inches. In this guide, the Sweetcrispy sits at 20 inches and the WLIVE three-drawer at 29.5. Measure your mattress first, including any topper, and test with a book at the planned height.

faq.q: Do I need a nightstand with charging?
faq.a: If you plug in more than one device, yes. The SONGMICS BELLAH has five ports, while the Sweetcrispy has none. A table without ports needs an extension lead near the bed, which is a trip hazard in the dark.

They hold light items such as books and chargers. Heavy objects belong on top, and the stated capacity on the listing is the limit. The BELLAH lists 66 lb for the whole table, the WLIVE two-drawer 55 lb. Spread the load across the top and drawers.
It is a nice-to-have. Models such as the Somdot, BOLUO and WLIVE RGB offer app or voice control. If you sleep with a bright room, skip it, and choose the Yoobure or BELLAH for charging.

Yes. Some, like the Sweetcrispy and the WLIVE two-drawer, list roughly 15 minute assembly. Check the listing for each, and allow time for the BELLAH's anti-tip kit. A drill speeds things up but is not required.

faq.q: How do I keep a nightstand from tipping?
faq.a: Use the anti-tip kit where provided, such as on the SONGMICS BELLAH, and adjust feet on uneven floors, as on the BOLUO. Keep heavy items low and avoid overloading the top drawer. A wall strap is worth the five minutes in a child's room.

finalTake: Buy the SONGMICS BELLAH if your bedside needs power for a phone, lamp and tablet. Choose the WLIVE three-drawer for a high bed and the Yoobure for certified wiring. The Sweetcrispy suits a low bed and a small budget, and the JOONEE a bedroom led by style. Match the height to your mattress first, then count what you plug in.
